newsitem.title: USA: Malcolm X widow to undergo fifth burn operation.
newsitem.headline: Malcolm X widow to undergo fifth burn operation.

text.p: The widow of Malcolm X, who was badly burned in a fire allegedly set by her troubled grandson, will undergo a fifth surgical procedure Wednesday, hospital officials said Tuesday.
"Betty Shabazz remains in extremely critical condition," a hospital spokeswoman said. Surgeons will perform Wednesday's operation if Shabazz's condition remains stable, she said.
Surgeons in the burn unit at Jacobi Medical Centre have already performed four operations to remove 72 percent of Shabazz's burned tissue.
During these operations, charred skin is replaced with Integra, an artifical skin product which helps the inner layer of skin heal enough to accept a permanent skin graft later.
Shabazz, 63, a celebrated civil rights activist, suffered third degree burns over 80 percent of her body in a fire set at her Yonkers, N.Y. apartment on June 1.
Malcolm Shabazz, 12, named after his controversial grandfather, was alleged to have splashed gasoline at the door of his grandmother's apartment and set it on fire.
The boy was living with his grandmother because his mother, Qubilah Bahiyah Shabazz, was concerned about the company he was keeping at her San Antonio, Texas home.
Malcolm was being held at a juvenile facility where he will undergo psyhological evaluation before next appearing in court.
